- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). ########## atomicfilewriter-temp-names.yaml
title: Simplify AtomicFileWriter and use clearer temporary file names
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins operator writing critical configuration files expects atomic writes to stay dependable and the resulting logs to be readable when the filesystem does not support true atomic moves, but the current implementation produces obscure temporary names and noisy duplicate failure reporting.


  ## Desired outcome

  `AtomicFileWriter` should create clearer temporary file names derived from the destination path and should remember after the first `AtomicMoveNotSupportedException` that the platform requires a non-atomic fallback. Once that fallback is known, Jenkins should replace the target cleanly without repeating the unsupported atomic attempt on every write.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Temporary files are easier to identify from their names, the first unsupported atomic move downgrades subsequent writes to the non-atomic replacement path, and operators no longer see duplicate stack traces caused by retry-and-rethrow logic when the filesystem lacks atomic move support.

  '
########## autocomplete-query-parameters.yaml
title: '[JENKINS-37241] Support for query parameters in autocomplete'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator or plugin author exposing an autocomplete field may need extra query parameters to scope the results, but the current autocomplete widget only sends the search term and makes it impossible to express that richer filtering contract.


  ## Desired outcome

  Autocomplete endpoints should be able to declare additional query parameters through the descriptor contract, and the browser widget should include them when fetching suggestions. This should let server-side autocomplete logic honor contextual filters without changing the visible widget behavior for fields that do not need extra parameters.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Autocomplete requests include any descriptor-defined extra query parameters alongside the typed term, existing fields without extra parameters keep working as before, and filtered suggestion endpoints can finally distinguish context that was previously unavailable to them.

  '
########## autocomplete-suggestion-count.yaml
title: Allow plugins to customize number of suggestions in autocomplete
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Some plugins need far more or far fewer autocomplete suggestions than Jenkins’s hard-coded default, but today they cannot express that preference in the rendered control.


  ## Desired outcome


  Plugin authors should be able to set the maximum suggestion count per autocomplete field without forking the widget.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The widget still defaults to 10 suggestions when nothing is specified, but a field can override that limit through the `data-maxsuggestions` attribute.

  '
########## background-discarder-logging.yaml
title: '[JENKINS-73692] Turn off logging from `BackgroundGlobalBuildDiscarder`'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  Background global build discarder maintenance can produce noisy per-job logging even when it is working normally, which makes administrative logs harder to scan.


  ## Desired outcome


  Keep the discarder behavior the same while removing routine chatter from its listener output.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The build discarder still evaluates jobs and applies matching retention strategies, but it no longer prints per-job progress lines for every processed job.

  '
########## backport-24622-ui-fixes.yaml
title: Backporting for 2.462.2
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  The 2.462.2 stabilization work included frontend fixes for add-item layouts, and users on the maintained line need the same polish instead of a visually inconsistent form experience.


  ## Desired outcome


  Backport the UI fixes so adding configurable blocks in Jenkins forms uses the corrected spacing and table styling from the stabilized release line.


  ## Acceptance signals


  Newly added items use the backported layout behavior instead of the older broken presentation, and the change stays confined to the front-end rendering of the add-item workflow.

  '
########## boot-version-logging.yaml
title: Print Jenkins version on boot
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins operator starting or upgrading a controller often needs to confirm from the startup logs exactly which Jenkins version is coming up, but boot logs do not currently state that version explicitly.


  ## Desired outcome

  When Jenkins starts, the normal startup log should include the controller version so administrators can confirm the running build without inferring it from package metadata or the UI. The boot message should clearly report the value returned by `Jenkins.getVersion()`.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Startup logs include a message containing the current Jenkins version during initialization, operators can confirm the running version from boot output alone, and no extra manual step is required to verify which release started.

  '
########## build-deletion-lts-backport.yaml
title: Backporting for 2.479.1 (part 3)
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator using build deletion, log rotation, or global build discarders expects running builds to be preserved until they have actually finished writing logs, but Jenkins can still try to delete a build while it is running or invoke discarding logic at the wrong point in finalization.


  ## Desired outcome

  Attempts to delete a running build must fail cleanly instead of partially removing it, with the user-visible message `Unable to delete <job> #<build> because it is still running`. Build discarding should run after finalization in a way that respects `isLogUpdated()`, avoids double-running job-level rotation, and only removes builds once Jenkins considers them finished.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Manual deletion of an active build is rejected with the exact `Unable to delete <job> #<build> because it is still running` message, log rotation skips builds whose logs are still being updated, and finalized builds are discarded once without duplicate job-level rotation passes.

  '
########## buildhistory-refresh-all-pages.yaml
title: '[JENKINS-73613] refresh buildhistory widget in all cases'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  The build history widget only refreshes reliably on the first page of results, so users looking at older pages can miss renamed builds, description changes, deletions, or updated running-build state until they manually reload.


  ## Desired outcome


  Build history should refresh whenever the page becomes active again and should keep the user on the same slice of history instead of snapping back to the top.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The widget refreshes on window focus, updates while viewing older pages, and preserves the current pagination context when reloading the build list.

  '
########## build-number-assigner.yaml
title: '`Job.BuildNumberAssigner`'
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Some Jenkins distributions and plugins need to customize how build numbers are allocated, but today the core logic is hard-wired inside `Job`.


  ## Desired outcome


  Expose a supported extension point for build-number assignment while still allowing the implementation to persist the next build number through a controlled callback.


  ## Acceptance signals


  `Job.BuildNumberAssigner` can supply the allocation strategy, `SaveNextBuildNumber` gives that strategy a way to persist the sequence, and the default Jenkins behavior remains the built-in fallback.

  '
########## buildwithparameters-303-redirects.yaml
title: '[JENKINS-66105] Allow follow redirects to work after 303 from `buildWithParameters`'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  Some API clients trigger parameterized builds and then follow the redirect returned by `buildWithParameters`, but today a 303 chain can land on a queue item URL that is not useful to generic HTTP clients.


  ## Desired outcome


  Following the redirect from `buildWithParameters` should end on a stable queue item endpoint that both human operators and automation can consume.


  ## Acceptance signals


  A client that follows the initial 201 and later 303 response reaches a 200 response, and the queue item landing page points callers to `api/json?tree=cancelled,executable[url]` for status details.

  '
########## cli-websocket-handshake-errors.yaml
title: Friendlier handling of `DeploymentHandshakeException` from CLI in `-webSocket` mode
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Users invoking the Jenkins CLI in `-webSocket` mode get an unhelpful failure when the WebSocket handshake is rejected, which makes authentication and reverse-proxy issues hard to diagnose.


  ## Desired outcome


  A handshake failure should tell the user what HTTP status came back and surface the response headers that matter for debugging.


  ## Acceptance signals


  On a rejected handshake the CLI prints `CLI handshake failed with status code 401`, includes headers such as `Server: Jetty` when available, and exits with status 15 instead of a generic stack trace.

  '
########## command-palette-header-guard.yaml
title: '`headerCommandPaletteButton` undefined when `JenkinsHeader` not loaded'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins page that does not render the standard `JenkinsHeader` should still be allowed to load frontend assets safely, but the Command Palette initializer currently assumes the header button exists and crashes on layouts that omit it.


  ## Desired outcome

  The Command Palette frontend should detect when `headerCommandPaletteButton` is absent and simply skip initialization on that page. Pages without `JenkinsHeader` should remain fully usable instead of failing because the palette tried to bind to a missing control.


  ## Acceptance signals

  On layouts without the standard header, the page loads without JavaScript errors, the palette code exits early when `headerCommandPaletteButton` is missing, and pages that do include the header keep the normal Command Palette behavior.

  '
########## command-palette-icons.yaml
title: Add icons to Command Palette
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins user searching from the Command Palette needs enough visual context to distinguish jobs, users, views, agents, and other results at a glance, but the current results list is text-only and forces people to infer the target type from the name alone.


  ## Desired outcome

  Search results returned to the Command Palette should include both an `icon` and a `type` so the frontend can render the right symbol for each result class. Jobs should expose meaningful status-based icons, and the palette should present those icons consistently across the different result types Jenkins exports.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Command Palette result payloads include `icon` and `type`, jobs surface a status-derived search icon, and users can visually distinguish result categories in the palette without opening each match first.

  '
########## command-palette-ui-refinement.yaml
title: Refine Command Palette UI
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins user opening the Command Palette expects it to feel responsive and polished, but the current dialog can show awkward loading flicker, abrupt closing behavior, and visual rough edges that make the interaction feel unfinished.


  ## Desired outcome

  The Command Palette should load results with smoother spinner timing, cleaner open-and-close animation, and more consistent spacing and visual treatment so it feels like a first-class navigation surface. The interface should preserve existing search behavior while improving the perceived responsiveness of searching and dismissing the palette.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The loading spinner appears only when searches take long enough to warrant it, closing the palette uses a deliberate transition instead of an abrupt disappearance, and the updated palette styling reads as a polished UI refinement rather than a functional regression.

  '
########## contextmenu-from-compatibility.yaml
title: '[JENKINS-73785] Restore `ContextMenu#from` with `StaplerRequest`/`Response` args'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  Some plugins and adjunct code still call the older `ContextMenu#from` overload that accepts `StaplerRequest` and `StaplerResponse`, and that compatibility path disappeared during the newer request-type migration.


  ## Desired outcome


  Restore the legacy overload so existing integrations continue to build and run while the ecosystem migrates to the new request types.


  ## Acceptance signals


  `ContextMenu#from(ModelObjectWithContextMenu, StaplerRequest, StaplerResponse)` is available again and delegates to the newer request and response implementation instead of forcing every caller to migrate immediately.

  '
########## deprecate-administrativemonitor-permission.yaml
title: Deprecate AdministrativeMonitor#getRequiredPermission
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Plugin authors still see `AdministrativeMonitor.getRequiredPermission()` as the obvious extension point even though newer permission-check helpers provide the safer contract Jenkins now expects.


  ## Desired outcome


  The older permission getter should remain available for compatibility but be clearly deprecated in favor of `checkRequiredPermission()` and `hasRequiredPermission()`.


  ## Acceptance signals


  Existing monitors continue to load, but developers are guided toward the newer helper methods instead of treating `getRequiredPermission()` as the preferred contract.

  '
########## deprecate-subtask-getlastbuilton.yaml
title: Deprecating `SubTask.getLastBuiltOn`
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Queue scheduling still exposes `SubTask.getLastBuiltOn` even though Jenkins no longer relies on it in a meaningful way, which encourages plugin authors to depend on stale behavior.


  ## Desired outcome


  Mark this API as deprecated and communicate that it is no longer part of the supported scheduling contract, without changing how queued work is assigned or how builds run today.


  ## Acceptance signals


  Existing callers still compile and run, the deprecated entry points remain available for compatibility, and normal build execution behavior stays unchanged.

  '
########## descriptor-newinstance-httpresponse.yaml
title: Tolerate `HttpResponse` thrown from `Descriptor.newInstance`
category: feature
requirement: '## Context


  Some descriptors intentionally abort instantiation by throwing an `HttpResponse`, for example to redirect or return a structured form response, but Jenkins currently risks wrapping that control flow as an internal instantiation failure.


  ## Desired outcome


  Descriptor creation should let intentional `HttpResponse` escapes propagate normally instead of turning them into linkage-style errors.


  ## Acceptance signals


  If `Descriptor.newInstance` encounters an exception that is also an `HttpResponse`, Jenkins preserves that response behavior; only true instantiation failures are wrapped and logged as such.

  '
########## detached-plugin-cache.yaml
title: Use detached plugins as a cache for the Update Center
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Initial setup and plugin installation can spend unnecessary time downloading plugin files that Jenkins already ships as detached plugins.


  ## Desired outcome


  Jenkins should treat detached plugins as a best-effort cache for Update Center downloads so setup is faster when the bundled copy already matches the expected checksums.


  ## Acceptance signals


  If a matching detached plugin is already available, Jenkins installs from that cached file instead of the network; if validation or lookup fails, installation falls back to the normal download path without user-visible breakage.

  '
########## detached-plugin-origin-logging.yaml
title: Note the plugin responsible for loading a detached plugin
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  When Jenkins auto-loads a detached plugin to satisfy an implied dependency, the current logging does not say which plugin caused that dependency to be pulled in.


  ## Desired outcome


  Operators should be able to see the originating plugin in the log message so dependency resolution is easier to audit.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The detached-plugin log line names both the detached plugin being loaded and the source plugin that required it.

  '
########## disable-yui-default.yaml
title: '[JENKINS-73539] Disable YUI by default'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator upgrading the UI stack should get the YUI-free experience by default, because keeping the legacy library enabled unless someone opts in slows the transition and leaves obsolete dependencies active longer than necessary.


  ## Desired outcome

  The `RemoveYuiUserExperimentalFlag` should default to enabled so Jenkins removes YUI from pages unless an administrator explicitly opts back out through the `jenkins.model.experimentalflags.RemoveYuiUserExperimentalFlag.defaultValue` system property. Pages that no longer rely on YUI, including the old debug log reader hook, should continue to load without that library being initialized.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Fresh and upgraded controllers default to the YUI-removed path, administrators can still override the default with the `jenkins.model.experimentalflags.RemoveYuiUserExperimentalFlag.defaultValue` system property, and pages no longer initialize the legacy YUI debug log reader by default.

  '
########## dosaferestart-compatibility.yaml
title: '[JENKINS-73838] Compatibility for `Jenkins#doSafeRestart(StaplerRequest, String)`'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  Older callers still invoke `Jenkins#doSafeRestart(StaplerRequest, String)`, and the newer request-type migration should not break those integrations abruptly.


  ## Desired outcome


  Keep a compatibility overload for the old safe-restart signature while steering new development toward the `StaplerRequest2` form.


  ## Acceptance signals


  `Jenkins#doSafeRestart(StaplerRequest, String)` remains available as a deprecated bridge and delegates correctly to the newer safe-restart implementation.

  '
########## dosaferestart-lts-backport.yaml
title: Backporting for 2.479.1 (part 4)
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Plugin or integration code that still calls the deprecated `doSafeRestart` overloads may pass a null request object in compatibility scenarios, and Jenkins currently throws before the restart flow can be delegated to the newer implementation.


  ## Desired outcome

  The deprecated `doSafeRestart(StaplerRequest)` and `doSafeRestart(StaplerRequest, String)` entry points should remain tolerant of `null` and forward that call through to the modern restart path without crashing. This is a compatibility fix for callers that still rely on those overloads in the 2.479.1 LTS line.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Calling either deprecated `doSafeRestart` overload with a null request no longer throws during request conversion, the restart path still reaches the current implementation, and existing LTS callers do not need to special-case null before invoking Jenkins.

  '
########## dosaferestart-null-compatibility.yaml
title: Allow for null to be passed to `doSafeRestart`
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Plugin or integration code that still calls the deprecated `doSafeRestart` overloads may pass a null request object in compatibility scenarios, and Jenkins currently throws before the restart flow can be delegated to the newer implementation.


  ## Desired outcome

  The deprecated `doSafeRestart(StaplerRequest)` and `doSafeRestart(StaplerRequest, String)` entry points should remain tolerant of `null` and forward that call through to the modern restart path without crashing. This is a compatibility fix for callers that still rely on those overloads.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Calling either deprecated `doSafeRestart` overload with a null request no longer throws during request conversion, the restart path still reaches the current implementation, and existing callers do not need to special-case null before invoking Jenkins.

  '
########## dropdown-reinitialization.yaml
title: Fix dropdowns being added multiple times to the same element
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context


  Some Jenkins pages can initialize the same dropdown host more than once, which produces stacked popovers and inconsistent interaction on a single control.


  ## Desired outcome


  Reinitializing a dropdown on an element should replace the previous dropdown instance instead of layering another one on top.


  ## Acceptance signals


  If the element already has a dropdown-themed `_tippy` instance, Jenkins destroys it before creating the new dropdown, so only one menu is attached to the element at a time.

  '
########## ee9-core-migration.yaml
title: '[JENKINS-73278] Migrate core from EE 8 to EE 9'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  Jenkins core must move from EE 8 to EE 9 to stay on supported platform dependencies, but plugin authors need a migration path that does not abruptly strand existing integrations.


  ## Desired outcome


  Core should adopt the Jakarta EE 9 stack while preserving compatibility bridges for established Jenkins extension APIs during the transition.


  ## Acceptance signals


  Jenkins exposes the EE9-oriented request and response contracts such as `StaplerRequest2` and `StaplerResponse2`, legacy entry points continue to delegate where possible, and existing plugins can keep running while they migrate to the new types.

  '
########## executors-widget-interfaces.yaml
title: Extract interfaces for objects to be used through the executors widget
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context


  The executors widget is tightly coupled to concrete controller-side classes, which makes it hard for alternate Jenkins distributions to present aggregated executor views while preserving core UI behavior.


  ## Desired outcome


  The widget should consume stable interfaces for computers, executors, and tasks so alternate implementations can participate without rewriting the whole page.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The widget can work with abstractions such as `IComputer`, `IExecutor`, `IDisplayExecutor`, and `ITask`, and the management UI still exposes actions like `Configure Monitors` and `Save` to the users who should see them.

  '
########## fips-password-length-validation.yaml
title: '[JENKINS-74858]  Added validation for Password length in FIPS mode'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator running with FIPS-compliant cryptography expects local user creation and password changes to reject passwords that are too short for that mode, but Jenkins currently allows values that should not be accepted under the stricter policy.


  ## Desired outcome

  When FIPS mode is enabled, HudsonPrivateSecurityRealm should reject passwords shorter than 14 characters during account creation and password updates, while still allowing valid matching passwords that meet the minimum. The validation should attach to the password field so users understand what must be corrected.


  ## Acceptance signals

  In FIPS mode, passwords under 14 characters are rejected, matching passwords of 14 or more characters succeed, and administrators no longer end up with locally managed credentials that violate the active compliance policy.

  '

########## administrativemonitor-at-since.yaml
title: Add missing at-since in AdministrativeMonitor
category: feature
requirement: '## Context


  The AdministrativeMonitor API recently gained manager-aware permission helpers, but its Javadoc still does not say which Jenkins version introduced them.

########## agent-protocols-config-removal.yaml
title: Removing configurability of `Jenkins.agentProtocols`
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator should not have to manually curate the list of built-in inbound agent protocols in the global security screen, because that configuration can drift away from the supported transport set and create confusion about what Jenkins actually allows.


  ## Desired outcome

  Jenkins should stop treating built-in agent protocols as an administrator-managed security setting and should instead expose the supported protocol set directly from core. The configuration UI and backing APIs should no longer offer agent protocol toggles that imply these built-in transports can be selectively disabled there.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The global security configuration no longer presents agent protocol selection as an editable admin setting, Jenkins reports the supported built-in protocols from core without relying on saved UI state, and upgrading preserves working agent connectivity without a manual protocol reconfiguration step.

  '
########## atomicfilewriter-temp-names.yaml
title: Simplify AtomicFileWriter and use clearer temporary file names
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins operator writing critical configuration files expects atomic writes to stay dependable and the resulting logs to be readable when the filesystem does not support true atomic moves, but the current implementation produces obscure temporary names and noisy duplicate failure reporting.


  ## Desired outcome

  `AtomicFileWriter` should create clearer temporary file names derived from the destination path and should remember after the first `AtomicMoveNotSupportedException` that the platform requires a non-atomic fallback. Once that fallback is known, Jenkins should replace the target cleanly without repeating the unsupported atomic attempt on every write.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Temporary files are easier to identify from their names, the first unsupported atomic move downgrades subsequent writes to the non-atomic replacement path, and operators no longer see duplicate stack traces caused by retry-and-rethrow logic when the filesystem lacks atomic move support.

  '
########## autocomplete-query-parameters.yaml
title: '[JENKINS-37241] Support for query parameters in autocomplete'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator or plugin author exposing an autocomplete field may need extra query parameters to scope the results, but the current autocomplete widget only sends the search term and makes it impossible to express that richer filtering contract.


  ## Desired outcome

  Autocomplete endpoints should be able to declare additional query parameters through the descriptor contract, and the browser widget should include them when fetching suggestions. This should let server-side autocomplete logic honor contextual filters without changing the visible widget behavior for fields that do not need extra parameters.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Autocomplete requests include any descriptor-defined extra query parameters alongside the typed term, existing fields without extra parameters keep working as before, and filtered suggestion endpoints can finally distinguish context that was previously unavailable to them.

  '
########## autocomplete-suggestion-count.yaml
title: Allow plugins to customize number of suggestions in autocomplete
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Some plugins need far more or far fewer autocomplete suggestions than Jenkins’s hard-coded default, but today they cannot express that preference in the rendered control.


  ## Desired outcome


  Plugin authors should be able to set the maximum suggestion count per autocomplete field without forking the widget.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The widget still defaults to 10 suggestions when nothing is specified, but a field can override that limit through the `data-maxsuggestions` attribute.

  '

title: '[JENKINS-73692] Turn off logging from `BackgroundGlobalBuildDiscarder`'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  Background global build discarder maintenance can produce noisy per-job logging even when it is working normally, which makes administrative logs harder to scan.


  ## Desired outcome


  Keep the discarder behavior the same while removing routine chatter from its listener output.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The build discarder still evaluates jobs and applies matching retention strategies, but it no longer prints per-job progress lines for every processed job.

########## boot-version-logging.yaml
title: Print Jenkins version on boot
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins operator starting or upgrading a controller often needs to confirm from the startup logs exactly which Jenkins version is coming up, but boot logs do not currently state that version explicitly.


  ## Desired outcome

  When Jenkins starts, the normal startup log should include the controller version so administrators can confirm the running build without inferring it from package metadata or the UI. The boot message should clearly report the value returned by `Jenkins.getVersion()`.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Startup logs include a message containing the current Jenkins version during initialization, operators can confirm the running version from boot output alone, and no extra manual step is required to verify which release started.

  '
########## build-deletion-lts-backport.yaml
title: Backporting for 2.479.1 (part 3)
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator using build deletion, log rotation, or global build discarders expects running builds to be preserved until they have actually finished writing logs, but Jenkins can still try to delete a build while it is running or invoke discarding logic at the wrong point in finalization.


  ## Desired outcome

  Attempts to delete a running build must fail cleanly instead of partially removing it, with the user-visible message `Unable to delete <job> #<build> because it is still running`. Build discarding should run after finalization in a way that respects `isLogUpdated()`, avoids double-running job-level rotation, and only removes builds once Jenkins considers them finished.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Manual deletion of an active build is rejected with the exact `Unable to delete <job> #<build> because it is still running` message, log rotation skips builds whose logs are still being updated, and finalized builds are discarded once without duplicate job-level rotation passes.

  '
########## buildhistory-refresh-all-pages.yaml
title: '[JENKINS-73613] refresh buildhistory widget in all cases'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  The build history widget only refreshes reliably on the first page of results, so users looking at older pages can miss renamed builds, description changes, deletions, or updated running-build state until they manually reload.


  ## Desired outcome


  Build history should refresh whenever the page becomes active again and should keep the user on the same slice of history instead of snapping back to the top.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The widget refreshes on window focus, updates while viewing older pages, and preserves the current pagination context when reloading the build list.

  '
########## build-number-assigner.yaml
title: '`Job.BuildNumberAssigner`'
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Some Jenkins distributions and plugins need to customize how build numbers are allocated, but today the core logic is hard-wired inside `Job`.


  ## Desired outcome


  Expose a supported extension point for build-number assignment while still allowing the implementation to persist the next build number through a controlled callback.


  ## Acceptance signals


  `Job.BuildNumberAssigner` can supply the allocation strategy, `SaveNextBuildNumber` gives that strategy a way to persist the sequence, and the default Jenkins behavior remains the built-in fallback.

  '
########## buildwithparameters-303-redirects.yaml
title: '[JENKINS-66105] Allow follow redirects to work after 303 from `buildWithParameters`'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  Some API clients trigger parameterized builds and then follow the redirect returned by `buildWithParameters`, but today a 303 chain can land on a queue item URL that is not useful to generic HTTP clients.


  ## Desired outcome


  Following the redirect from `buildWithParameters` should end on a stable queue item endpoint that both human operators and automation can consume.


  ## Acceptance signals


  A client that follows the initial 201 and later 303 response reaches a 200 response, and the queue item landing page points callers to `api/json?tree=cancelled,executable[url]` for status details.

  '
########## cli-websocket-handshake-errors.yaml
title: Friendlier handling of `DeploymentHandshakeException` from CLI in `-webSocket` mode
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Users invoking the Jenkins CLI in `-webSocket` mode get an unhelpful failure when the WebSocket handshake is rejected, which makes authentication and reverse-proxy issues hard to diagnose.


  ## Desired outcome


  A handshake failure should tell the user what HTTP status came back and surface the response headers that matter for debugging.


  ## Acceptance signals


  On a rejected handshake the CLI prints `CLI handshake failed with status code 401`, includes headers such as `Server: Jetty` when available, and exits with status 15 instead of a generic stack trace.

  '
########## command-palette-header-guard.yaml
title: '`headerCommandPaletteButton` undefined when `JenkinsHeader` not loaded'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins page that does not render the standard `JenkinsHeader` should still be allowed to load frontend assets safely, but the Command Palette initializer currently assumes the header button exists and crashes on layouts that omit it.


  ## Desired outcome

  The Command Palette frontend should detect when `headerCommandPaletteButton` is absent and simply skip initialization on that page. Pages without `JenkinsHeader` should remain fully usable instead of failing because the palette tried to bind to a missing control.


  ## Acceptance signals

  On layouts without the standard header, the page loads without JavaScript errors, the palette code exits early when `headerCommandPaletteButton` is missing, and pages that do include the header keep the normal Command Palette behavior.

  '
########## command-palette-icons.yaml
title: Add icons to Command Palette
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins user searching from the Command Palette needs enough visual context to distinguish jobs, users, views, agents, and other results at a glance, but the current results list is text-only and forces people to infer the target type from the name alone.


  ## Desired outcome

  Search results returned to the Command Palette should include both an `icon` and a `type` so the frontend can render the right symbol for each result class. Jobs should expose meaningful status-based icons, and the palette should present those icons consistently across the different result types Jenkins exports.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Command Palette result payloads include `icon` and `type`, jobs surface a status-derived search icon, and users can visually distinguish result categories in the palette without opening each match first.

  '
########## command-palette-ui-refinement.yaml
title: Refine Command Palette UI
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins user opening the Command Palette expects it to feel responsive and polished, but the current dialog can show awkward loading flicker, abrupt closing behavior, and visual rough edges that make the interaction feel unfinished.


  ## Desired outcome

  The Command Palette should load results with smoother spinner timing, cleaner open-and-close animation, and more consistent spacing and visual treatment so it feels like a first-class navigation surface. The interface should preserve existing search behavior while improving the perceived responsiveness of searching and dismissing the palette.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The loading spinner appears only when searches take long enough to warrant it, closing the palette uses a deliberate transition instead of an abrupt disappearance, and the updated palette styling reads as a polished UI refinement rather than a functional regression.

  '
########## contextmenu-from-compatibility.yaml
title: '[JENKINS-73785] Restore `ContextMenu#from` with `StaplerRequest`/`Response` args'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  Some plugins and adjunct code still call the older `ContextMenu#from` overload that accepts `StaplerRequest` and `StaplerResponse`, and that compatibility path disappeared during the newer request-type migration.


  ## Desired outcome


  Restore the legacy overload so existing integrations continue to build and run while the ecosystem migrates to the new request types.


  ## Acceptance signals


  `ContextMenu#from(ModelObjectWithContextMenu, StaplerRequest, StaplerResponse)` is available again and delegates to the newer request and response implementation instead of forcing every caller to migrate immediately.

  '
########## deprecate-administrativemonitor-permission.yaml
title: Deprecate AdministrativeMonitor#getRequiredPermission
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Plugin authors still see `AdministrativeMonitor.getRequiredPermission()` as the obvious extension point even though newer permission-check helpers provide the safer contract Jenkins now expects.


  ## Desired outcome


  The older permission getter should remain available for compatibility but be clearly deprecated in favor of `checkRequiredPermission()` and `hasRequiredPermission()`.


  ## Acceptance signals


  Existing monitors continue to load, but developers are guided toward the newer helper methods instead of treating `getRequiredPermission()` as the preferred contract.

  '
########## deprecate-subtask-getlastbuilton.yaml
title: Deprecating `SubTask.getLastBuiltOn`
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Queue scheduling still exposes `SubTask.getLastBuiltOn` even though Jenkins no longer relies on it in a meaningful way, which encourages plugin authors to depend on stale behavior.


  ## Desired outcome


  Mark this API as deprecated and communicate that it is no longer part of the supported scheduling contract, without changing how queued work is assigned or how builds run today.


  ## Acceptance signals


  Existing callers still compile and run, the deprecated entry points remain available for compatibility, and normal build execution behavior stays unchanged.

  '
########## descriptor-newinstance-httpresponse.yaml
title: Tolerate `HttpResponse` thrown from `Descriptor.newInstance`
category: feature
requirement: '## Context


  Some descriptors intentionally abort instantiation by throwing an `HttpResponse`, for example to redirect or return a structured form response, but Jenkins currently risks wrapping that control flow as an internal instantiation failure.


  ## Desired outcome


  Descriptor creation should let intentional `HttpResponse` escapes propagate normally instead of turning them into linkage-style errors.


  ## Acceptance signals


  If `Descriptor.newInstance` encounters an exception that is also an `HttpResponse`, Jenkins preserves that response behavior; only true instantiation failures are wrapped and logged as such.

  '
########## detached-plugin-cache.yaml
title: Use detached plugins as a cache for the Update Center
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Initial setup and plugin installation can spend unnecessary time downloading plugin files that Jenkins already ships as detached plugins.


  ## Desired outcome


  Jenkins should treat detached plugins as a best-effort cache for Update Center downloads so setup is faster when the bundled copy already matches the expected checksums.


  ## Acceptance signals


  If a matching detached plugin is already available, Jenkins installs from that cached file instead of the network; if validation or lookup fails, installation falls back to the normal download path without user-visible breakage.

  '
########## detached-plugin-origin-logging.yaml
title: Note the plugin responsible for loading a detached plugin
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  When Jenkins auto-loads a detached plugin to satisfy an implied dependency, the current logging does not say which plugin caused that dependency to be pulled in.


  ## Desired outcome


  Operators should be able to see the originating plugin in the log message so dependency resolution is easier to audit.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The detached-plugin log line names both the detached plugin being loaded and the source plugin that required it.

  '
########## disable-yui-default.yaml
title: '[JENKINS-73539] Disable YUI by default'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator upgrading the UI stack should get the YUI-free experience by default, because keeping the legacy library enabled unless someone opts in slows the transition and leaves obsolete dependencies active longer than necessary.


  ## Desired outcome

  The `RemoveYuiUserExperimentalFlag` should default to enabled so Jenkins removes YUI from pages unless an administrator explicitly opts back out through the `jenkins.model.experimentalflags.RemoveYuiUserExperimentalFlag.defaultValue` system property. Pages that no longer rely on YUI, including the old debug log reader hook, should continue to load without that library being initialized.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Fresh and upgraded controllers default to the YUI-removed path, administrators can still override the default with the `jenkins.model.experimentalflags.RemoveYuiUserExperimentalFlag.defaultValue` system property, and pages no longer initialize the legacy YUI debug log reader by default.

  '
########## dosaferestart-compatibility.yaml
title: '[JENKINS-73838] Compatibility for `Jenkins#doSafeRestart(StaplerRequest, String)`'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  Older callers still invoke `Jenkins#doSafeRestart(StaplerRequest, String)`, and the newer request-type migration should not break those integrations abruptly.


  ## Desired outcome


  Keep a compatibility overload for the old safe-restart signature while steering new development toward the `StaplerRequest2` form.


  ## Acceptance signals


  `Jenkins#doSafeRestart(StaplerRequest, String)` remains available as a deprecated bridge and delegates correctly to the newer safe-restart implementation.

  '
########## dosaferestart-lts-backport.yaml
title: Backporting for 2.479.1 (part 4)
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Plugin or integration code that still calls the deprecated `doSafeRestart` overloads may pass a null request object in compatibility scenarios, and Jenkins currently throws before the restart flow can be delegated to the newer implementation.


  ## Desired outcome

  The deprecated `doSafeRestart(StaplerRequest)` and `doSafeRestart(StaplerRequest, String)` entry points should remain tolerant of `null` and forward that call through to the modern restart path without crashing. This is a compatibility fix for callers that still rely on those overloads in the 2.479.1 LTS line.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Calling either deprecated `doSafeRestart` overload with a null request no longer throws during request conversion, the restart path still reaches the current implementation, and existing LTS callers do not need to special-case null before invoking Jenkins.

  '
########## dosaferestart-null-compatibility.yaml

category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Plugin or integration code that still calls the deprecated `doSafeRestart` overloads may pass a null request object in compatibility scenarios, and Jenkins currently throws before the restart flow can be delegated to the newer implementation.


  ## Desired outcome

  The deprecated `doSafeRestart(StaplerRequest)` and `doSafeRestart(StaplerRequest, String)` entry points should remain tolerant of `null` and forward that call through to the modern restart path without crashing. This is a compatibility fix for callers that still rely on those overloads.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Calling either deprecated `doSafeRestart` overload with a null request no longer throws during request conversion, the restart path still reaches the current implementation, and existing callers do not need to special-case null before invoking Jenkins.

  '
########## dropdown-reinitialization.yaml
title: Fix dropdowns being added multiple times to the same element
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context


  Some Jenkins pages can initialize the same dropdown host more than once, which produces stacked popovers and inconsistent interaction on a single control.


  ## Desired outcome


  Reinitializing a dropdown on an element should replace the previous dropdown instance instead of layering another one on top.


  ## Acceptance signals


  If the element already has a dropdown-themed `_tippy` instance, Jenkins destroys it before creating the new dropdown, so only one menu is attached to the element at a time.

  '
########## ee9-core-migration.yaml
title: '[JENKINS-73278] Migrate core from EE 8 to EE 9'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  Jenkins core must move from EE 8 to EE 9 to stay on supported platform dependencies, but plugin authors need a migration path that does not abruptly strand existing integrations.


  ## Desired outcome


  Core should adopt the Jakarta EE 9 stack while preserving compatibility bridges for established Jenkins extension APIs during the transition.


  ## Acceptance signals


  Jenkins exposes the EE9-oriented request and response contracts such as `StaplerRequest2` and `StaplerResponse2`, legacy entry points continue to delegate where possible, and existing plugins can keep running while they migrate to the new types.

  '
########## executors-widget-interfaces.yaml
title: Extract interfaces for objects to be used through the executors widget
category: refactor
requirement: '## Context


  The executors widget is tightly coupled to concrete controller-side classes, which makes it hard for alternate Jenkins distributions to present aggregated executor views while preserving core UI behavior.


  ## Desired outcome


  The widget should consume stable interfaces for computers, executors, and tasks so alternate implementations can participate without rewriting the whole page.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The widget can work with abstractions such as `IComputer`, `IExecutor`, `IDisplayExecutor`, and `ITask`, and the management UI still exposes actions like `Configure Monitors` and `Save` to the users who should see them.

  '
########## fips-password-length-validation.yaml
title: '[JENKINS-74858]  Added validation for Password length in FIPS mode'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator running with FIPS-compliant cryptography expects local user creation and password changes to reject passwords that are too short for that mode, but Jenkins currently allows values that should not be accepted under the stricter policy.


  ## Desired outcome

  When FIPS mode is enabled, HudsonPrivateSecurityRealm should reject passwords shorter than 14 characters during account creation and password updates, while still allowing valid matching passwords that meet the minimum. The validation should attach to the password field so users understand what must be corrected.


  ## Acceptance signals

  In FIPS mode, passwords under 14 characters are rejected, matching passwords of 14 or more characters succeed, and administrators no longer end up with locally managed credentials that violate the active compliance policy.

  '
########## flightrecorder-buffer-size.yaml
title: Reduce default size of diagnostic buffer for `FlightRecorderInputStream` from 1MiB to 1KiB
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator debugging CLI remoting failures needs the diagnostic ring buffer to preserve enough recent bytes to explain protocol corruption, but the current recorder is too small and can lose the context needed to troubleshoot intermittent failures.


  ## Desired outcome

  `FlightRecorderInputStream` should keep a larger default capture window and continue to make that size configurable through the `hudson.remoting.FlightRecorderInputStream.BUFFER_SIZE` system property. When CLI protocol parsing fails, the diagnostic output should retain enough recent traffic to make the corruption actionable.


  ## Acceptance signals

  The default recorder keeps a substantially larger recent byte history, operators can still override it with the `hudson.remoting.FlightRecorderInputStream.BUFFER_SIZE` property, and CLI corruption logs include enough buffered data to diagnose the failure instead of truncating the useful context.

  '
########## heterolist-scroll-into-view.yaml
title: scroll fields from added hetero-list entry into viewport
category: feature
requirement: '## Context


  When a user adds a new hetero-list entry containing many fields, Jenkins may leave the newly added content partly off-screen, forcing manual scrolling before the user can continue.


  ## Desired outcome


  The form should automatically bring the newly added block into view in a browser-native way, including tall entries that extend beyond the viewport.


  ## Acceptance signals


  After adding an entry, the relevant fields are scrolled into view instead of being hidden below the fold, and the behavior works without relying on the old YUI viewport helpers.

  '
########## idiomatic-python-style.yaml
title: Follow idiomatic Python coding style
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  The small Python maintenance script in this repository does not follow the project’s current Python style, which makes future edits noisier than they need to be.


  ## Desired outcome


  Align the script with idiomatic Python naming and environment checks without changing what the tool does.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The script behaves the same as before, but contributors see standard Python-style names and CI detection logic when they maintain it.

  '
########## inbound-agent-websocket-default.yaml
title: Add -webSocket option by default when creating an inbound agent
category: feature
requirement: '## Context


  The Jenkins UI still generates inbound agent launch commands that omit WebSocket mode unless the user notices and adds it manually, even though WebSocket is the safer default for many modern installations and reverse-proxy setups.


  ## Desired outcome


  The generated inbound-agent command should include WebSocket mode by default so new agents start with the recommended connection mode.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The launch snippet produced for an inbound agent includes `-webSocket` even when the user has not toggled an extra option.

  '
########## inbound-remoting-version-bypass.yaml
title: '[JENKINS-73467] No facility to try unsupported Remoting versions when using inbound agents'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context


  Some administrators intentionally allow older inbound remoting clients during upgrades, but WebSocket inbound agents still advertise the minimum supported version in a way that blocks those transitional rollouts.


  ## Desired outcome


  When the unsupported-remoting escape hatch is enabled, inbound agents connecting over WebSocket should be able to attempt the connection instead of being rejected up front by the version header.


  ## Acceptance signals


  If `SlaveComputer.ALLOW_UNSUPPORTED_REMOTING_VERSIONS` is true, the WebSocket agent endpoint no longer sends the minimum-version header that preemptively blocks the agent; otherwise the existing safeguard remains in place.

  '
########## item-creation-error-message.yaml
title: Fix error message when creation of item by type is prohibited
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context


  When Jenkins blocks creation of an item or view type for permission reasons, the error message includes a malformed permission path that repeats internal permission text and confuses administrators.


  ## Desired outcome


  The denial should name the missing permission and target type cleanly so the user understands what access is required.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The message format reads as `Job/Create/<type>` or `View/Create/<type>` without the duplicated permission token that was previously appended.

  '
########## item-deletion-preflight-hook.yaml
title: '`ItemListener.onCheckDelete` & `ItemDeletion.cancelBuildsInProgress`'
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Plugins sometimes need to veto deletion before Jenkins starts canceling queue items or interrupting running builds, but the current deletion flow does not offer a dedicated preflight hook.


  ## Desired outcome


  Item deletion should expose a pre-delete extension point and centralize the logic that cancels in-flight work, while keeping the observable deletion safeguards the same.


  ## Acceptance signals


  `ItemListener.onCheckDelete(Item)` runs before deletion work starts and can stop the operation, `ItemDeletion.cancelBuildsInProgress` owns the build-cancellation behavior, and users still see the same protection against deleting items with builds that cannot be stopped cleanly.

  '
########## javadoc-api-version-markers.yaml
title: Update version numbers of new APIs in Javadoc
category: feature
requirement: '## Context


  Recent public Jenkins APIs were added with placeholder or inaccurate version markers, which makes it harder for plugin developers to know when they can rely on them.


  ## Desired outcome


  The Javadoc for the newly introduced APIs should report the correct released version without changing runtime behavior.


  ## Acceptance signals


  The affected public APIs keep the same names and semantics, but their `@since` documentation points to the correct release.

  '
########## jenkins-load-view-recovery.yaml
title: Recover views after error in `Jenkins.load`
category: ci
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins administrator reloading configuration from disk expects a failed reload to leave the current view layout intact, but an exception during unmarshal can corrupt the in-memory view list and even leave `primaryView` in a broken recursive state.


  ## Desired outcome

  If configuration reload fails partway through, Jenkins should restore the original `views` collection and `primaryView` before rethrowing the error so the running controller remains navigable. Administrators should get the reload failure, but not lose access to their existing view configuration because of that failed attempt.


  ## Acceptance signals

  A reload failure does not wipe or corrupt the current view list, `primaryView` is restored to the pre-reload value instead of remaining null or recursive, and the controller stays usable after the failed reload while still surfacing the original error.

  '
########## jetty-12-ee8-upgrade.yaml
title: '[JENKINS-73130] Upgrade core from Jetty 10.x to 12.x (EE 8)'
category: ci
requirement: '## Context


  Jenkins needs the Jetty 12 EE8 upgrade to stay on supported infrastructure, but operators and plugin developers cannot absorb a server upgrade that silently breaks uploads, WebSocket settings, or existing compatibility knobs.

  The runtime should move to Jetty 12 EE8 while preserving established Jenkins behavior and keeping existing multipart tuning properties usable during the transition.

  The WebSocket provider honors `jenkins.websocket.idleTimeout`, non-WebSocket requests are still rejected cleanly, and the legacy multipart property names `RequestImpl.FILEUPLOAD_MAX_FILES`, `RequestImpl.FILEUPLOAD_MAX_FILE_SIZE`, and `RequestImpl.FILEUPLOAD_MAX_SIZE` continue to map to the new `MultipartFormDataParser` limits.

  '
########## keyboard-scroll-selection.yaml
title: Fix scrolling with keyboard
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A Jenkins user navigating Command Palette results with the keyboard expects arrow-key movement to keep the selected item visible, but the current scroll helper can miss cases where the selected element is undefined and keyboard navigation becomes unreliable.


  ## Desired outcome

  Keyboard-driven navigation should tolerate the absence of a selected item and only try to scroll when a real selection exists. The Command Palette should continue to wire keyboard handling only while it is open so arrow-key navigation stays smooth instead of tripping over an uninitialized selection.


  ## Acceptance signals

  Using the keyboard to move through Command Palette results no longer throws or stalls when nothing is selected yet, scrolling resumes once an item is actually selected, and navigation remains scoped to the palette while it is open.

  '
########## lifecycle-boot-failure.yaml
title: '`Lifecycle.onBootFailure`'
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  Alternate Jenkins lifecycle implementations can react to restart and shutdown events, but they are not told when the controller fails during boot.


  ## Desired outcome


  Lifecycle providers should receive an explicit boot-failure callback so environments that rely on process supervision or auto-restart can handle startup failures intentionally.


  ## Acceptance signals


  A failed startup calls `Lifecycle.onBootFailure(BootFailure)`, and lifecycles such as the exit-based implementation can respond by restarting or terminating according to their policy.

  '
########## lts-24793-zip-installer.yaml
title: Backporting for 2.479.3 LTS (part 3)
category: other

  '
########## makebutton-jenkins-button.yaml

category: ci

  `makeButton` should create a standard `jenkins-button` element while keeping just enough compatibility for legacy callers to continue working during the migration.

  '
########## manage-monitor-visibility.yaml
title: Allow administrative monitors to be displayed for users with `Overall/MANAGE` permission
category: other

  Jenkins administrators with `Overall/MANAGE` but not `Overall/SYSTEM_READ` can still be responsible for day-to-day controller health, yet some administrative monitors disappear entirely for them.

  '
########## modernize-build-trend-page.yaml
title: modernise build time trend page
category: other
requirement: '## Context


  The build time trend page still feels dated and inconsistent, and it does not clearly express whether agent information is part of the table for the current job type.


  ## Desired outcome


  The page should use the modern table and button presentation while still working for both classic abstract projects and newer job types.

  The rendered table advertises its layout with `data-show-agent=false` or `data-show-agent=true`, timestamps are shown in the refreshed UI, and console and build links remain directly usable.

  '
########## nodelistener-oncreated-initialization.yaml
title: Ensure NodeListener#onCreated is called once the Node initialization is complete
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  Plugin developers using `NodeListener#onCreated` expect the callback to run only after the new node is fully initialized, because creation handlers may immediately read filesystem-backed node state. Jenkins currently fires the event too early for that contract to be safe.


  ## Desired outcome

  When a node is first created, Jenkins should complete registration and `onLoad` initialization before invoking `NodeListener#onCreated`. A creation listener should be able to access initialization-dependent state such as `node.getRootDir()` without tripping over a partially loaded node.


  ## Acceptance signals

  `NodeListener#onCreated` fires only after the node has been inserted and loaded, listeners can safely touch initialization-dependent state like `node.getRootDir()` during creation handling, and plugins no longer need to defer basic created-node work to avoid premature callbacks.

  '
########## npm-lint-autofix.yaml

  '
########## offline-api-since-annotations.yaml

########## offline-by-design-ui.yaml
